name: Ken Burns effect
summary: A slow pan and zoom across a still image, so that a photograph moves in a film.
how: Move 5% to 15% of the frame over 4 to 8 seconds on each still.
Start or end each move on a face or on the key detail.

origin.note: Ken Burns pans and zooms over still photographs in a documentary series; rostrum-camera moves are older.

adoptions.via: Apple names the pan-and-zoom setting after Burns in its photo and video software.
Video essays move a slow zoom of 3% to 6% over a still or a clip.
Photo-mode slideshows zoom and pan slowly over each still image.
